lead: The least populated neighbourhood in Barcelona: an enclave of houses of rural origin between El Carmel, La Vall d'Hebron and Horta.
text: La Clota is one of the oldest settlements in Horta-Guinardó. It arose on the plain of Can Tarrida, a 13th-century farmhouse (masia) that disappeared when Avinguda de l'Estatut was opened, with plentiful water, vegetable gardens and a well at every house, and from the mid-19th century until well into the 20th it was the neighbourhood of the washerwomen. In 2021 the City Council plenary gave provisional approval to the amendment of the general plan for the neighbourhood, which protects its landscape, its agricultural heritage and its old paths, and provides for 134 more homes, 30% of them officially protected housing.

Its urban growth has been very limited, which is why it keeps a semi-rural character: many houses are of rural origin and have names of their own, such as Ca la Bugadera Rica, Cal Reig and Can Curé, alongside self-built homes, workshops and warehouses. With 1,123 inhabitants in just 0.18 km², it is the least populated neighbourhood in Barcelona, and its average sale price, 4,668 €/m², is the highest in Horta-Guinardó. Because it is so small, the price and rent figures rest on few transactions and should be treated with caution. If you are selling, the average sale price is 35% above the Horta-Guinardó average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 373,000 € on average, and this is one of the most expensive neighbourhoods in Horta-Guinardó (1st of 11 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (1,074 €/month) is 18% above the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Houses of rural origin and self-built homes in a small hillside enclave, with very limited supply.
